reason: The checker question is 'which declaration does this identifier resolve to, and does that declaration start after this use?'. getSymbolAtLocation handles shadowing, hoisted function declarations (allowed), imports and export specifiers. Syntax can only relate an identifier to a later declaration when both sit inside one pattern (the port catches `var a = b, b;`). Metavariables are not shared across `precedes`/`inside`, so 'identifier X ... later `var X` / `import X`' cannot be written. A same-name match would still be wrong under shadowing, which needs real binding resolution.

evidence.why: `var i = j;` is flagged only because `var j` is declared at line 32 of the same scope; the use and the declaration are unrelated statements
`console.log(foo1)` inside a function refers to an `import { default as foo1 }` that appears later; resolving the import binding needs a scope graph
export specifier `undeclaredA` resolves via getExportSpecifierLocalTargetSymbol to a later `var undeclaredA`
